comment: Every name C++ drives in the sky's materials. Mirrors Source/DeepSpace/Sky/SkyMaterialContract.h; Tools/setup_sky_materials.py authors from it and DeepSpace.Sky.MaterialContract holds the header, this file and the built assets to the same lists. Keys under 'parameters' are roles the authoring script wires by; 'name' is the only place the Unreal name is written.
ground_comment: M_SkyGround: unlit, M_SkyBody's own law (the light, the colour, the brightness, the 1.5 disc gain, the terminator's smoothstep, the face clamp) and M_SkyBody's own face, composed by the same surface() graph from the shared file's terms; its normal is the tile's vertex normal (UV1.xy, UV2.x, universe axes) plus the pixel's slope of only the bands the vertices do not carry (WR_GroundNormal). BandLimit (the tile's spacing over R) and TilePivot (the tile's pivot from the world's centre, cm) are custom primitive data, so one instance serves every tile. World Position Offset lowers each vertex by (1 - Morph) x its height (UV2.y, km) along its direction: the relief grows in between the handover and the drive floor. No rim: the sky is black.

shared_relief.comment: M_SkyBody's face as one Custom node over Shaders/Private/WorldRelief.ush, the file the C++ compiles too (landing decision 1). SkyMaterialContract.h holds the same include, entry and pins; DeepSpace.Sky.MaterialContract holds the built nodes to them, and the file's tables to this file's constants.

shadow.comment: The cast shadow (baked, not marched): M_SkyBody, M_SkyGround and M_SkyShadowProbe each call the world's map through one Custom node over the shared file -- WR_ShadowMapCoord for the texel coordinates and the level (and Night, under PsiLo, where the map is 0), WR_ShadowTapsAt for the four texels at each of two levels, WR_Bilinear and WR_Lerp to blend them, eight Loads of ShadowMap -- and then lerp(map, Vertex, Morph): the body passes Vertex 1 and Morph 0, the ground its UV0.x and its Morph. Footprint is one pixel's: the body and the ground pass their face's footprint over filter_pixels, the probe ProbeFootprint as it is. SkyMaterialContract.h holds the same entry and pins; DeepSpace.Sky.MaterialContract holds the built nodes to them. default_texture is what a world without a map reads, white.

meshes.comment: SM_SkyBody: the sphere every body and neighbour is drawn with, built by UDeepSpaceEditorScripting::BuildSkySphere as an equal-angle cube sphere, one LOD per entry of cells_per_lod, finest first. SkySphereMesh.h decides the screen size each LOD switches at, from the view it is sized for: no facet more than half a 4K pixel inside the limb. 224 is what LOD 0 needs at the nearest the sky ever draws a world, 1.6e-3 of its radius; each coarser LOD halves the cells and takes over once it is far enough away not to show.

constants.surface_comment: M_SkyBody's face: noise on the unit direction in object space, so every frequency is in cycles per body radius. One coarse band of continent_levels octaves at level_scale (continents and basins, or the belts' wander), then one detail band per octave from there down to the finest, each a single octave at its own weight. The engine halves every octave inside a multi-octave band, so detail built that way arrives fainter the nearer the world is -- and the last decade of an approach, the one that says whether the ship is close, got the faintest. Flat weights make every octave read as strongly when it arrives as the first did. Every octave fades out by the pixel footprint once its wavelength is under filter_pixels, so what shows is always what the screen can hold. surface_max_swing bounds the face at 1 +/- it times the smooth disc, whatever the CVars say: the half-float ceiling is never nearer than it was.
constants.relief_comment: M_SkyBody's relief: the ground's own slope (landing decision 3) -- ReliefScale is FWorldRelief::SlopeScale, PeakCm / (R x SMax), so the orbit shades exactly the heights a ship lands on; giants, which have no ground, keep a fixed cloud-top billow (ShipSky::GiantReliefScale, 0.066, a C++ constant: the 0.2 x 0.33 giants were drawn with before landing; nothing here sets it), oceans none. Craters are summed compact kernels, one per kept site (WR_CraterSum): one band per crater_frequencies entry, a site kept in crater_keep of the cells, crater_radius cells wide, its profile crater_depth deep in scale with a rim crater_rim of it; the bands step by four, so the count wider than D goes as D^-2, the highlands' law. Their albedo is fewer in the basins (maria_cratering of the highlands'); their height is the same everywhere, so the orbit shades the ground a ship lands on. Craters darken their floors and brighten their rims by the albedo terms, behind the same half-float guard as the face.
constants.probe_comment: Eyes.WorldReliefParity's probes: D over a fixed patch -- normalize(centre + (u - 0.5) span east + (v - 0.5) span north), the three an orthonormal frame.
